procedure.description: panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 15847 (panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen) with date of service 2026-07-02. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: The documentation does not establish a functional impairment or failure of conservative treatment of the skin condition.

criteria.text: Panniculus hangs at or below the level of the pubis (grade 2 or higher) as documented on examination.

Recurrent or chronic intertrigo, cellulitis, or skin breakdown beneath the panniculus that has failed at least 3 months of conservative treatment such as topical antifungals, hygiene measures, and barrier products.
Weight stable within 10 pounds for at least 6 months.
The panniculus interferes with activities of daily living or ambulation.

chart.text: Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

63 year old man here about the abdominal apron after his weight loss. Nice result on the weight. Discussed panniculectomy versus a full abdominoplasty and what insurance will and will not look at. His history otherwise: migraines, rare now, prediabetes, diet controlled. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Quit smoking 4 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. On exam the pannus hangs well below the pubis, I would call it grade 3, with maceration and an odor in the fold. He has been fighting the rash under the apron for better than a year, treated with nystatin, then clotrimazole, keeps it dry with powder and a cloth liner, and it comes right back. Two rounds of antibiotics from the PCP for cellulitis in the fold. Down 147 pounds since the sleeve in 2024 and still losing, 199 today. Says he cannot walk more than a block without the skin fold chafing raw, has to lift it to wash underneath, cannot find pants that fit over it.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 217, LDL 122, HDL 54, triglycerides 157. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 3 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Follow-up on the abdomen. Went back over the operation, drains, the scar, recovery of four to six weeks. He understands this is skin and fat removal for the skin problems, not a tummy tuck. Vitals today 120 over 70, pulse 80. Rash is back again despite 8 months of the antifungal and barrier routine. Fold is red and weeping today. Weight 184 today, down another 15 from last visit. Still losing steadily.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.6, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Blood pressure check. 128 over 72 today, 137 over 78 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, he remains sure about going ahead.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the resection with him standing. Nicotine negative. Hold the metformin the morning of.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-3 (weight) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan or a shortfall, not completed treatment or a met threshold.
